title: Selectively Uniform Concurrency Testing
problem: Randomized concurrency testing algorithms fail to uniformly sample thread interleavings, causing them to miss bugs that manifest only in rare, infrequent interleavings. Prior algorithms are biased in their sampling, leading to poor coverage of the exponentially large interleaving space.
motivation: Concurrent program bugs are elusive because they appear in only a small fraction of possible thread interleavings, and existing randomized testing tools systematically under-explore these rare cases.
method: SURW (Selectively Uniform Random Walk) is an online randomized concurrency testing algorithm that achieves interleaving-uniformity by carefully selecting a subset of program events and applying a uniform sampling strategy over their interleaving space. The algorithm operates as a black-box randomized technique that requires only minimal additional information about the program to achieve uniformity over broad classes of programs and arbitrary event subsets.
key_novelty: First black-box randomized concurrency testing algorithm to provably achieve interleaving-uniformity for a wide class of programs, enabling systematic exploration of rare buggy interleavings.
contributions: Theoretical proof that uniform sampling over interleaving space is achievable with minimal additional program information
SURW algorithm achieving interleaving-uniformity for broad program classes and arbitrary event subsets
Demonstration of more bugs exposed and faster bug discovery than comparable randomized algorithms on leading concurrency benchmarks
Empirical validation of superior interleaving-space and behavior-space exploration uniformity on real-world programs

metrics.other: More bugs exposed and faster than comparable randomized algorithms on leading concurrency benchmarks

limitations: Not discussed; the specific classes of programs for which uniformity is guaranteed are not detailed in the abstract.
primary_theme: Uniform randomized concurrency testing for rare bug discovery
